title: Cop31 collapses: why did climate talks fall apart? - The Latest
summary_full: Countries at the Cop31 climate summit failed to reach a keystone agreement for the first time in 17 years. The talks, co-chaired by Turkey and Australia, were intended to produce a pact that would have injected urgency into climate action and financing for vulnerable states. Instead, the deal failed after a standoff over fossil fuels and support for countries exposed to the climate crisis. Guardian Australia’s climate and environment reporter Graham Readfearn tells Lucy Hough why there are calls for urgent reform of the Cop process – watch on YouTube Continue reading...
